facts.text: Bowling Green is famed as the 'cradle of American horse racing' and houses Virginia’s second‑oldest Masonic Lodge.
The town took its name from founder Dache Carmine’s plantation, whose land and funds built the courthouse when it became county seat in 1803.
Old Mansion, a pre‑Georgian house built around 1741, remains the oldest continuously inhabited residence in Virginia.
A major freight railroad line that once belonged to Virginia now runs through Bowling Green as part of CSX, while Amtrak trains also pass through.
Strolling down Bowling Green’s tree‑lined streets, you’ll find locally owned shops like Artism by Joey and JB Apothecary, showcasing community creativity.
The historic district, anchored by Old Mansion, includes colonial landmarks listed on both the Virginia Landmarks Register and the National Register of Historic Places.
